title: The duplicate that crossed a tenant boundary
blurb: A global similarity index leaked and weak pairs bridged clusters.
prompt: A tenant's dedupe check confirmed that another tenant held the same customer record, and two unrelated records merged because one weak pair bridged them. The draft checks membership and insert non-atomically. Review it, fix it, and prove comparison stays in-tenant and merges carry evidence.
aiNote: The draft runs fuzzy comparisons against a global index, so a check can confirm whether another tenant holds the same record and even name it, and it unions clusters transitively through any weak pair, letting low-confidence links collapse unrelated groups.
testIdea: Check a record that exists for another tenant and assert a miss; build A-B strong and B-C weak and assert A and C never share a cluster without review; race two identical submissions and assert one winner.
followUps: What confidence should a merge require?
How do you undo a bad merge?
When is exact-only matching actually enough?
